question: I want RDS high availability where the standby also handles read queries. Which deployment type is that, and how many standbys does it have?

gold.answer: A Multi-AZ DB cluster deployment: it has two standby DB instances (three Availability Zones) that provide failover and can also serve read traffic, unlike the single-standby Multi-AZ DB instance deployment.

question: I need WORM protection for seven years on objects in an existing unversioned S3 bucket. What must be turned on first, and which Object Lock mechanism fits a fixed period?

gold.answer: Enable S3 Versioning first, because Object Lock works only on versioning-enabled buckets. Then use a retention period, fixed via a retain-until-date, optionally as the bucket's default retention; a legal hold is for indefinite protection.

With fixed retention, you specify the retain-until-date.

question: An IAM user in a member account has AdministratorAccess, but an SCP on the account denies all of S3. Can they create a bucket, and would the same SCP restrict the management account's administrator?

gold.answer: No bucket: effective permissions are the intersection of what the SCP allows and what identity policies allow, so S3 is denied. The management account is unaffected because SCPs apply only to member accounts.

question: My RDS Multi-AZ DB instance deployment has a standby, so I will point reporting queries at the standby to offload reads. Which endpoint do I use?

question: RDS read replicas are billed at a discounted replica rate, aren't they?

gold.answer: No. Read replicas are billed as standard DB instances at the same rates as the instance class used for the replica; only same-Region replication data transfer is free.

question: Once an S3 object version is under an Object Lock retention period, nobody can upload a new version with the same key, correct?

gold.answer: No. Retention periods and legal holds protect only the locked version; new versions can still be created and delete markers added on top of the object.
support: Retention periods and legal holds don't prevent new versions of the object from being created, or delete markers to be added on top of the object.

question: Each S3 object version stores only the diff from the previous one, so versioning barely costs more. Is that right?

gold.answer: No. Each version is the entire object, not a diff, and normal rates apply to every version; three versions of an object are charged as three objects.
support: Each version of an object is the entire object; it is not just a diff from the previous version.
